children: It isn't just Nvidia that is reeling following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday.
Shares of several companies with ties to the $4 trillion chip maker were dropping as investors wondered what Huang's exit means for the artificial-intelligence trade.
CoreWeave fell 6.8% on Thursday. Nvidia holds a 12.8% stake in the AI cloud-computing provider, and is also its most important supplier.
It's a major reversal for the stock, which rallied 25% on Wednesday thanks to solid third-quarter earnings that helped ease some of the market's worries about the company's debt load.
Other AI players were also struggling Thursday. Shares of key supplier Super Micro Computer dropped 12%.

Nvidia also holds stakes in AI cloud provider Nebius, chip maker Intel, Finnish telecom provider Nokia, and silicon chip designer Synopsys. All those stocks were falling on Thursday. Some others didn't drop: Optical networking company Coherent rose 0.3%, rocket and AI company SpaceX added 2.1%, and silicon chip designer Synopsys traded flat.
The AI trade enjoyed a revival on Wednesday as CoreWeave's earnings after the bell Tuesday reassured investors that demand for products tied to the AI buildout remains robust.

Huang's exit could spark a reassessment, though. Nvidia has been a sort of central banker to the whole AI trade — and the worry is his eventual permanent successor may not be so willing to dip into their pockets.
Huang resigned as president, CEO, and board member on Thursday, effective immediately. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO.
Huang's departure came following revelations about his personal conduct. Multiple reports said he had two extramarital affairs.
One affair was with a suspected Chinese spy and another was with an employee, The Wall Street Journal reported. Huang acknowledged he had been unfaithful in a letter to staff earlier this week.
Nvidia didn't immediately respond to Barron's request for comment.
